tag_values_meta.description: Canonical tag value lists for OSM tag support tracking. Values sourced from OSM wiki key pages and explicit consumer usage. sources[] lists wiki and/or engine_ids that explicitly handle the value. taginfo_count is the global in_ways count (all way types, proxy for highway use). Edit this file to adjust categories, add notes, or remove spurious entries.

issues.note: Overview issue explicitly listing tracktype, smoothness, sac_scale, and mtb:scale as the key difficulty tags to address for track/path rendering. The most relevant upstream thread for all tracked tag gaps in Americana.

notes: surface= is included as a raw OSM string value in the streets layer. Shortbread does not normalize or reclassify values. Any legal OSM surface value, including laterite, will appear in the tile if present on the way.

notes: Not in the Shortbread v1.0 attribute set. sac_scale is not exported; consumers cannot use it for styling without a custom tile pipeline.

evidence.summary: Shortbread v1.0 schema documentation listing the streets layer attributes including surface as a string field.
Streets layer documentation confirming surface attribute is included; smoothness, tracktype, sac_scale, and mtb:scale are not listed.

notes.Both rendering properties must be active: alpineHiking=true (enables the alpine overlay) AND alpineHikingScaleScheme=sacScale (selects SAC coloring vs CAI or other schemes).

notes: The comment at line 1325 notes that the color convention deviates from the Swiss alpine hiking map convention the SAC scale originates from. T1 (hiking) is black; T2-T3 are magenta; T4-T6 are purple.
When showSurfaceGrade=true is also active, the stroke width on paths widens to accommodate the colored overlay alongside the sac_scale band.

evidence.summary: showSurfaces renderingProperty declaration — "Road surface" toggle that enables the surface color overlay.
routeInfo_surface renderingAttribute with 23 explicit surface=* cases; laterite is absent from this list.
apply_if showSurfaces block for highway=track that enables the surface color overlay lane.
tracktype grade1-5 pathEffect values (solid/10_3/5_3/3_3/2_3) applied to highway=track, always-on.

effects.value: distinct color (orange or yellow hue, difficulty indicator)

notes: Organic Maps renders hiking difficulty on the map without requiring the user to toggle a special mode; sac_scale coloring is always-on for visible paths.
Exact color values differ from the OsmAnd convention. Colors are theme-dependent (day/night).

evidence.summary: Tag-to-type classifier; determines which surface/tracktype/sac_scale values get encoded into .mwm types that the renderer reads.
Default map style files (lines.sty or equivalent); define line colors, widths, and dash patterns per road/path type.
Reads surface, tracktype, smoothness and applies math.min speed caps.
surface_speeds table for car profile.
tracktype_speeds table for car profile.
smoothness_speeds table for car profile.

issues.title: Path with mountain_hiking creates weird snapping on foot profile
issues.note: sac_scale=mountain_hiking caused routing anomalies; no dedicated sac_scale support exists in OSRM.

notes: SAC_scale_limit default 3; any SAC above limit gets access penalty 9000.
Below limit, penalty uses K1=0.05 / K2=0.6 multipliers relative to SAC_scale_preferred (default 1).
Falls back to mtb:scale if sac_scale absent.

evidence.summary: ispaved and isunpaved derived from surface and smoothness.
tracktype-based penalties for track-like ways.
smoothness penalty table and wet-condition branches.
smoothness estimation from tracktype.

issues.title: SAC scale cost
issues.note: Feature request to add sac_scale penalty support to hiking profiles. Currently only hiking-mountain.brf handles it.

notes: Only sac_scale=hiking keeps default speed (5 km/h); all other values drop to SLOW_SPEED (2 km/h).
sac_scale also encoded as metadata rating 1-6 by OSMHikeRatingParser for custom model filtering.

evidence.summary: Tracktype speed mapping for tracks.
Bad surface speed capping logic.
Reads surface and tracktype, merges by min speed and applies smoothness factor.
Unknown tagged surface can force pushing speed.

issues.title: Add support for sac_scale=strolling in hike_rating path details
issues.note: sac_scale=strolling is a valid OSM value but missing from the hike_rating encoded value.

evidence.summary: Explicit precedence, surface and tracktype win over smoothness.
tracktype mapped to surface enum when no surface tag.
Fallback surface inference from road class/use.
Surface-based cost penalties and speed factors in bicycle costing.

issues.title: Cycling on sac_scale tagged ways
issues.note: Bicycle access logic on sac_scale ways is still incorrect after the

evidence.summary: Documentation states merged integrity from smoothness, surface, and tracktype.
Tracktype and smoothness penalty values.
prefer_unpaved branch with many tracktype/surface multipliers.
Bicycle profile block with smoothness/tracktype/surface multipliers.

issues.title: More support of SAC and CAI scale hiking difficulty
issues.note: Request for sac_scale to influence routing decisions, not just rendering. Current routing.xml lacks sac_scale routing logic.

notes: Access behavior for high sac_scale values in bicycle mode is not fully verified. The type classifier likely blocks sac_scale >= alpine_hiking from routable types.
Organic Maps has a dedicated "hiking" app mode that enables routing on harder trails. The exact sac_scale thresholds differ between the pedestrian and hiking profiles.

evidence.summary: OSM tag to internal type classifier; defines which surface/tracktype values affect routing speed and access classification at map compile time.
Bicycle routing logic; references road class types that encode surface quality.
Tag classifier; encodes sac_scale values into routable vs non-routable hiking path types.
Pedestrian/hiking routing; road class types that sac_scale feeds into.

notes: Appears in highway=path and highway=via_ferrata presets.

evidence.summary: Default preset XML defining combo fields for surface, smoothness, tracktype, sac_scale, and mtb:scale across highway, track, and path dialogs.
Preset format documentation describing combo, list, and text field types used to construct the editor UI.

notes: Present in the highway=path preset, typically as a secondary field.
iD shows the OSM wiki description for each value when the field is focused.

evidence.summary: Field definition for surface=* as a combo type with all standard values listed.
Field definition for smoothness=* with all 9 standard values.
Field definition for tracktype=* with grade1-grade5.
Field definition for sac_scale=* with all 6 hiking difficulty values.

notes: Present in highway=path presets.

evidence.summary: Source repository for the Vespucci default preset, maintained in JOSM-compatible XML format. Includes combo fields for surface, smoothness, tracktype, sac_scale, and mtb:scale.
Vespucci documentation explaining the preset-based editing workflow and Properties editor for arbitrary tags.

effects.value: shown with photo illustration and difficulty description

notes: Each answer button includes a short explanation of the difficulty level, making this one of the most mapper-friendly UIs for sac_scale.

Layer definition for cycling infrastructure; includes surface question with image-select widget.

notes: No quest exists. Issue

evidence.summary: Quest definition for road surface; defines eligibility filter, answer set, and how selected values are written as OSM tags.

issues.title: Quest for sac_scale
issues.note: Long-standing open request. Complexity of the SAC scale definition has been cited as a barrier to implementation.

notes: Not used in the current openstreetmap-carto style. Paths are rendered uniformly regardless of sac_scale value. Dedicated outdoor map styles (e.g. OpenTopoMap, Waymarked Trails) do use sac_scale for path coloring.

evidence.summary: CartoCSS file defining road line styles; includes surface-based unpaved detection and tracktype-based dash patterns for highway=track.

issues.title: Introduce sac_scale and trail_visibility on highway=path
issues.note: Open PR proposing rendering for demanding hiking difficulty levels (demanding_mountain_hiking and above). Stalled since January 2023 over reviewer concerns about tag consistency.

notes: Not styled in the current Americana style. The style has a US focus and outdoor hiking difficulty scales are lower priority.

evidence.summary: JavaScript module defining road line styles including surface-based paved/unpaved classification and tracktype-based dash patterns.
MapLibre GL style definition; road layer rules reference surface and tracktype attributes from the underlying vector tiles.
